record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Which off-policy evaluation method can estimate or rank candidate offline reinforcement learning policies robustly enough to work across a wide variety of datasets, so that practitioners can trust it for policy evaluation or model selection instead of relying on environment rollouts?

evidence.quote: Ultimately, in real-world settings, we often cannot roll out our policy to evaluate if it will work or not. This is a considerable barrier to the practical use of offline RL methods since we still rely too heavily on simulator rollouts to verify that a method works. Therefore, having robust OPE methods that work reliably across a wide variety of datasets is essential for advancing the field.

Levine et al. [8] argued that shifting toward off-policy selection instead of the evaluation was a promising direction for OPE methods. While we have seen this shift occur with the introduction of the DOPE benchmark, we still lack a method that can consistently outperform the others on most datasets.

artifact.category_tag: Off-policy evaluation in offline reinforcement learning
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting. A Markov decision process is given by a tuple $(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},P,r,\gamma,ho_0)$ with state space $\mathcal{S}$, action space $\mathcal{A}$, unknown transition kernel $P(s'\mid s,a)$, reward function $r:\mathcal{S}	imes\mathcal{A}	o\mathbb{R}$, discount factor $\gamma\in[0,1)$, and initial-state distribution $ho_0$. The value of a policy $\pi:\mathcal{S}	o\Delta(\mathcal{A})$ is
$$V(\pi)\;=\;\mathbb{E}\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}\,r(s_t,a_t)\;\Big|\;s_0\simho_0,\;a_t\sim\pi(\cdot\mid s_t),\;s_{t+1}\sim P(\cdot\mid s_t,a_t)ight].$$
An off-policy evaluation (OPE) procedure is a map $\widehat{V}$ that, given only a static dataset $\mathcal{D}=\{(s_i,a_i,r_i,s'_i)\}_{i=1}^{N}$ generated by one or more unknown behavior policies, and a target policy $\pi$, returns either an estimate $\widehat{V}(\pi;\mathcal{D})\in\mathbb{R}$ of $V(\pi)$ or, given a finite set of candidate policies $\{\pi_1,\dots,\pi_K\}$, a ranking of them by predicted return (off-policy selection).

Question. Design and analyze an OPE / off-policy selection procedure $\widehat{V}$ with the following robustness property: there exist explicit, broadly applicable conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ (e.g. coverage, behavior-policy diversity, function-class assumptions) under which, uniformly across a wide family $\mathcal{F}$ of MDPs and dataset-generating distributions, the procedure achieves
(i) a finite-sample bound $|\widehat{V}(\pi;\mathcal{D}) - V(\pi)| \le \varepsilon(N,\delta,\mathcal{F})$ with probability $1-\delta$, with $\varepsilon	o 0$ as $N	o\infty$, and/or
(ii) a high-probability guarantee that the top-ranked policy among $\{\pi_1,\dots,\pi_K\}$ has value within $\eta$ of $\max_k V(\pi_k)$,
in such a way that the procedure consistently dominates existing OPE estimators (e.g. importance sampling, fitted-Q evaluation, doubly-robust, model-based, and stationary-distribution-ratio methods) on standard benchmark distributions of datasets. Equivalently: does there exist a single OPE method whose worst-case ranking/estimation error over a broad class of offline datasets and policies is provably smaller than that of every existing OPE method, eliminating the need for environment rollouts for policy selection?
artifact.status_search_result: As of recent literature on the DOPE benchmark and follow-up OPE/off-policy selection work, no single off-policy evaluation or selection method has been shown to consistently outperform competitors across diverse offline RL datasets; robust, dataset-agnostic OPE remains an acknowledged open problem in the offline RL community.

status_evidence.title: Benchmarks for Deep Off-Policy Evaluation (DOPE)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces DOPE benchmark and shows that no current OPE method dominates across tasks and datasets.
status_evidence.claim: The DOPE benchmark demonstrates that current OPE methods have inconsistent performance across datasets, leaving robust OPE open.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: We still lack a method that can consistently outperform the others on most datasets.
status_evidence.claim: Robust dataset-agnostic OPE/off-policy selection is identified as an unresolved direction.
